standard.title: Selecting and preparing food
standard.description: explore how food can be selected and prepared for healthy eating
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have explored how plants and animals are grown for food (AC9TDE2K03). They can identify plant and animal food sources. They have not yet organised foods into health categories or connected preparation methods to healthy eating outcomes.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explore how foods can be selected and prepared for healthy eating, identifying food groups and preparation methods.

nodes.label: Selecting foods for healthy eating
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify a range of foods and categorise them into food groups for healthy eating
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least three familiar foods and categorise them into food groups using the Australian Guide to Healthy Eating
nodes.typical_width: Identify a wide range of foods and categorise them into the 5 food groups; discuss ways to eat a variety of food groups; begin to design a simple menu that includes multiple food groups
wider: Explore both the Australian Guide to Healthy Eating and the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Guide to Healthy Eating — identify foods in each of the 5 food groups from both guides; compare foods that are familiar to different communities
Explore how people from countries of Asia select food for healthy eating based on available plants and animals and cultural practices — identify similarities and differences with the Australian guide
Explore the local supermarket to observe the variety and placement of foods — consider how shelf design may influence food selection for healthy eating

response_modes.reason: Students readily categorise foods they personally eat but struggle with the full range of food groups when their exposure is narrow. Multiple food contexts — including foods from First Nations and Asian food traditions — builds a richer, less culturally narrow understanding of 'healthy eating'.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The dual guide direction (Australian and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander) is genuinely rich — it makes visible that healthy eating is culturally situated and that both guides share the same nutritional principles. This is pedagogically valuable beyond categorisation.
success_criteria: Correctly categorises at least three foods into food groups
Names at least two different food groups

nodes.label: Preparing food for healthy eating
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explore different ways food can be prepared and connect preparation methods to healthy eating
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two ways food can be prepared (e.g. raw, steamed, roasted, sliced); explain how preparation changes the food
nodes.typical_width: Explore different preparation methods (raw, steaming, roasting, slicing, cooking) and how each changes the food's flavour, texture or nutritional value; prepare a simple food product using appropriate tools and equipment; connect preparation choices to healthy eating
wider: Prepare vegetables in different ways (e.g. raw salad versus roasted) — compare the changes in flavour and texture and discuss how preparation affects how we experience food
Prepare a food product from a school kitchen garden, farmers' market or supermarket — identify the preparation steps, tools needed and connect to healthy eating

response_modes.reason: Food preparation involves procedural skills — safe handling, correct use of tools, following steps in order. These require practice across multiple preparation tasks to build the consistent safety habits and procedural fluency needed. Consolidation is the primary response; width adds preparation contexts.

success_criteria: Names at least two preparation methods
Explains how at least one preparation method changes the food
